sections.skill: Identify personal and sensitive information before sharing

questions.prompt: Which detail is personal information?

choices.text: The capital city of a country
A recipe for vegetable soup
A full name with a home address
The name of a famous public monument

questions.correct_answer: A full name with a home address
questions.intro: Before pasting text into an AI tool, scan it for PERSONAL INFORMATION: details that identify a person, such as a full name with an address, phone number, email, birth date, student or employee ID, or a photo of a face. Some information is SENSITIVE: it could cause harm if exposed, such as health conditions, government ID numbers, bank or card numbers, passwords, precise location, immigration status or private messages. Data can also identify someone in COMBINATION: "the only left-handed tuba player in our school" may point to one person. Once shared, you may not control where the information goes.

questions.intro: A quick SCAN finds most personal details. Read the text once looking only for: NAMES of private people, NUMBERS (phone, ID, account, date of birth), PLACES tied to a person (home address, exact location), CONTACT details (email, social media handles) and HEALTH or MONEY facts about someone. Mark each one. Example: "Call Rosa Diaz at 555-0199 about her bill." Marked: Rosa Diaz (name), 555-0199 (phone), "her bill" (money fact). Anything marked should be removed or replaced if the task does not need it.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Find personal information in hidden places

questions.prompt: Jon pastes an email thread for a summary. Where might hidden personal details be?

choices.text: Only in attachments he did not paste
Nowhere; threads are anonymous
In signatures and the "to" and "cc" lines
Only in the subject line

questions.correct_answer: In signatures and the "to" and "cc" lines
questions.intro: Personal information hides in places people forget: email signatures, the "to" and "cc" lines of a pasted thread, file names, screenshots with notifications showing, document metadata, and photos that show house numbers or school logos. Information about OTHER people, such as a friend's diagnosis in a group chat you paste, deserves the same care as your own. When unsure, treat a detail as sensitive and remove it, or ask whether the task actually needs it.
questions.feedback: Headers and signatures hold contact details.
